title: First Light results from PARAS: The PRL Echelle Spectrograph
what_was_studied: First-light design and stabilized simultaneous-reference measurements
numerical_result: The paper reports 370 to 860 nm coverage, resolving power near 63000, 0.04 deg C short-term temperature stability and 3.7 m/s short-term radial-velocity stability; 1 m/s was a future vacuum-enclosure expectation rather than an achieved result
remaining_question: How much of the short sequence transfers across later detector, enclosure and calibration epochs?

title: The PRL stabilized high resolution echelle fiber-fed spectrograph
what_was_studied: Detailed hardware description and first radial-velocity results
numerical_result: PARAS provides roughly 380 to 950 nm in one exposure at resolving power near 67000; RV extraction uses the 380 to 690 nm region
remaining_question: What is the long-baseline zero-point stability after interventions?

title: Precision wavelength calibration for radial velocity measurements using uranium lines
what_was_studied: Uranium hollow-cathode reference construction and line selection for PARAS
numerical_result: The study characterizes uranium calibration lines between 380 and 690 nm for precision RV use
remaining_question: How does uranium calibration compare with simultaneous ThAr on identical stellar exposures?

title: PARAS instrument description
what_was_studied: Instrument environment, coverage and standard-star performance summary
numerical_result: PRL reports 1.7 m/s over two years for sigma Draconis and 3.5 m/s for HD 55567, with better than 2 m/s on bright standards in selected data
remaining_question: The undated page does not establish current observing availability or a uniform all-target precision
